chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about salat (prayer) in saline marshland, and he disliked it because the forehead does not settle evenly. So I said: If there is level ground in it? He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer being asked about
key_terms.الْجَبْهَةَ: the forehead, specifically in relation to sajdah
key_terms.فَكَرِهَهُ: he disliked it, indicating karahah rather than prohibition
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it, indicating permissibility
key_terms.مُسْتَوِيَةً: level or even, describing proper ground for placing the forehead

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in a saline marshland or uneven ground?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing salat (prayer) in saline or uneven ground. It indicates dislike when the place of prostration is not level enough for the forehead to rest properly, but permits prayer there if a level spot is available.
